gradeRuling.question: Is the v1.9 review's ACCEPT-AS-CANDIDATE at 0 blockers, with applyRecommendation DO-NOT-APPLY-UNTIL-CORPUS-RESOLVER-CHECK, application-grade under D-001's route-A acceptance property once the named condition is discharged?
gradeRuling.ruling: FOR APPLICATION — the proposed reading SURVIVES this adversarial attempt to refute it. The objections above are against the entry's chain narration and motion specification, not against the ruling; none reopens the grade question.
reviewBytesEvidence: The disposition writes an unconditional bar and a conditional one in the same breath: 'Accept as candidate. Do not seal; do not apply until a corpus resolver (check-completeness.py or -v2) has positively resolved the chain, which freeze 7.3 requires and which no review substitutes for.' (recommendationToTheCoordinator.disposition). Sealing gets a bare prohibition; application gets an until-clause naming the exact instruments that later ran POSITIVE. The reviewer demonstrably knew how to write an unconditional bar and chose not to for application.

whatIDidNotCheck[7] verbatim: 'Freeze 7.3 requires a positive corpus-resolver run before APPLYING any derivation; my resolver's success does not substitute. This is the one gate still owed before application, hence the apply recommendation.' — 'the ONE gate still owed before application' quantifies the owed set at exactly one, and its subject is APPLICATION, not candidacy-reconsideration. This sentence directly refutes the AGAINST reading's claim that the until-clause governs only when candidacy may be reconsidered.

None of the six advisories conditions application. A-R19-01: 'It does not affect the validity of the act.' A-R19-02/03/04/05 route every repair to 'a successor'. A-R19-06's repair field grades the no-instrument/no-freeze-pin posture 'Correct posture for CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED; recorded so the absence is not read as a review omission' — descriptive of the current posture and routed to 'a successor', never stated as a bar on the coordinator's apply act.

No sentence anywhere in the review's 244 lines imposes candidate-only language beyond the label: no 'a coordinator must not', no fresh-acceptance-required clause, no condition on any other row. Swept for 'candidate' (verdict.recommendation, disposition's first sentence, A-R19-06's posture line, and the artifact-id — nothing else), for 'apply/application' (the until-clause, whatIDidNotCheck[7], and A-R19-06's freeze-7.8 aside that a green checker run 'would be author-side evidence anyway' — which concerns evidence weight, not permission), and for imperatives addressed to the coordinator.
gradeRuling.propertyTextAnalysis: D-001 T2-02 explicates 'no express reservation' as three prohibitions and maps them one-to-one onto its three precedents: 'EIR v6: accepted as CANDIDATE only' ↔ no candidate-only limitation; 'delivery.v5: expressly not for application' ↔ no EXPRESSLY-NOT-FOR-APPLICATION language; 'r1 v1.9: apply-condition chain' ↔ no named apply-condition LEFT UNDISCHARGED on the record. The candidate label cannot be what any class turns on, because it is common to the precedents: delivery.v5's verdict reads (measured this session) 'AS A CANDIDATE, AND EXPRESSLY NOT FOR APPLICATION. Zero blockers', and EIR v6's read 'ACCEPT AS A CANDIDATE -- 0 BLOCKERS' — yet the property assigns the three to three different classes. What distinguishes them is the language BEYOND the label: v6 routes nowhere (no apply path at all — promotion was never contemplated), v5 routes AROUND application (express refusal), v1.9 routes TO application (a dischargeable until-clause). Only under this reading does the qualifier 'left undischarged on the record' do any work; the AGAINST reading makes it dead text for the very precedent that defines its class. Symmetrically, the FOR reading does NOT render 'no candidate-only limitation' vacuous for future until-clause verdicts: a verdict that couples an until-clause with candidate-ONLY language ('even after X, a fresh acceptance is required') stays disqualified — the test is whether the verdict's own words route to application or around it.
counterEvidenceWeighed: The label itself, and the imperative 'Accept as candidate.' — real, and insufficient alone for the reasons above.

corpus-resolution.v2's consequence line lists 'ACCEPT-AS-CANDIDATE with six advisories, do not seal' among 'the independent review's other standing conditions … untouched' — but that record declares binds: 'NOTHING', and its same list continues 'applying is a separate coordinator act', and its caveat sentence expressly contemplates 'a coordinator applying v1.9 on this record'. It is the chain's own record contemplating exactly the act D-005 proposes.

DR-204 adjudication 5 characterizes EIR v6's 'ACCEPT AS A CANDIDATE -- 0 BLOCKERS' as 'candidate-grade, an express reservation under the route-A acceptance property' — the closest adjudicated authority for the AGAINST reading. Distinguished on its facts: v6's verdict was the label ALONE, with no apply routing of any kind (the adjudication's own contrast case, EIR v12, turned on 'zero reservation-language hits', and neither ruling addresses an until-clause verdict). Decisively, ruling 4 of the SAME adjudication rules 'DR-009/R09 reliance on this review — including the corpus-resolution.v2 (f79ccd04…, POSITIVE) link in the R09 chain — is clean' — a ruling with no purpose if the label barred application regardless of the chain.

Plain 'ACCEPT' existed in this corpus before the v1.9 review (TM storage-namespace v4: 'ACCEPT, 0 blockers', 2026-08-04; retention-tiers.v26 'ACCEPT at 0 blockers'), so the reviewer had the stronger word available. Weighed and outweighed: the corpus's own application law (freeze §3 TM row) is 'a reviewer accepts it and a coordinator applies it' — acceptance-as-candidate was the standard grade under which v1.6, delivery.v4 and C-2 v11 were all lawfully applied, and the v1.9 reviewer's OWN explanation of the label's operative content is the until-clause plus 'the one gate still owed before application'.

The §7.1 'no retained checker … disqualifying for application' residual is scoped by its own words to the EIR byte-recipe lineage ('this lineage never received a companion instrument'; §7.8 opens by naming it 'the residual §7.1 grades disqualifying' and calls the wall reading a misreading).
